summary: Proposes Multilink Protocol Plus (MP+), an extension to the PPP Multilink Protocol for managing multiple data links bundled together. It is informational and describes a vendor protocol.

eli5.summary: Several small roads can be combined to act like one big road. This describes a vendor way to manage those bundled roads.

questions: how does mp+ add and remove channels
how does mp+ remote management work
subtitle: Adding session management to bundled network links

tldr.problem: The PPP Multilink Protocol (MP) bundles multiple links for greater bandwidth but lacks session and link management capabilities. Operators and endpoints need to dynamically add and remove links as bandwidth requirements change.
tldr.mechanism: MP+ adds an in-band control channel and state machine to negotiate version information, request link additions or removals, manage phone numbers for dialing, and allow remote device management.
tldr.outcome: Network administrators can now dynamically adjust bundled connections and remotely manage unconfigured systems, providing better bandwidth control without reconfiguring the entire session.

today: RFC 1934 is Informational and describes a vendor-specific Ascend protocol. It extends the standard PPP Multilink Protocol (RFC 1990) but has not been widely adopted beyond Ascend communications equipment.

sections.title: Introduction to MP+
sections.content:
RFC 1934 describes Multilink Protocol Plus (MP+), an extension to the PPP Multilink Protocol. The basic MP bundles multiple independent links between two systems to create one virtual link with greater combined bandwidth.

MP+ adds a new inband control channel on top of MP that enables session management without requiring link reconfiguration. It lets administrators negotiate version compatibility, dynamically add and subtract channels as bandwidth needs change, and remotely manage unconfigured devices.
sections.eli5: MP bundles several phone lines into one big connection. MP+ adds a control line to that bundle so both sides can talk about adding or removing lines without disconnecting everything.

sections.title: MP+ Architecture and Layers
sections.content:
MP+ splits into two functional layers: a reliable delivery layer and a call management layer. The reliable delivery layer handles an error-control state machine with just three states (Stopped, Idle, Pending) and a simple acknowledge-and-retry mechanism for control messages.

The call management layer is the source and sink of MP+ control messages and handles the session state machine with major states: Initial (unused session), Idle (active but inactive), Add (adding channels), Remove (removing channels), and Close (terminating).

A key principle is that MP+ only consumes bandwidth when actively performing operations like adding or removing links, not during idle operation.
sections.eli5: MP+ is built in two parts: one makes sure control messages arrive safely, and the other decides what to do with them (add lines, remove lines, etc.).

sections.title: Control Messages and Frame Format
sections.content:
MP+ control messages are carried inside PPP frames with a Protocol ID of 0x0073. Each message type has a numeric identifier (1-16) representing operations like VERSION_EXCHANGE, ADD_REQ/ADD_RSP, REMOVE_REQ/REMOVE_RSP, CLOSE_REQ/CLOSE_RSP, and remote management messages.

The VERSION_EXCHANGE message starts a session by informing the peer of protocol version, session identifier, hardware type, and mode information. The ADD and REMOVE messages handle bandwidth adjustments: ADD_REQ requests additional channels and includes phone numbers to dial; REMOVE_REQ requests channel removal. Each request gets a response, and a COMPLETE message confirms the operation finished.

Remote management messages (REMOTE_MGMT_REQ, REMOTE_MGMT_RX_REQ, REMOTE_MGMT_TX_REQ) allow a master station to manage a slave station by sending commands and receiving output before normal network configuration is complete. A CLEAR_REQ message initiates friendly shutdown.
sections.eli5: Control messages are numbered orders: version exchange to say hello, add/remove requests to change line count, and management messages to configure a remote device.

sections.title: State Machines and Operation
sections.content:
The reliable delivery layer operates a simple three-state machine: when a DATA message is transmitted, the layer enters Pending and waits for an ACK. If the ACK arrives, it acknowledges the current transmission number and moves to Idle. If a retransmit timer expires before the ACK, the message is resent up to a configurable RETRANSMIT_COUNT limit. Upon reaching the limit, an error is reported and the state machine returns to Start.

The call management layer's state machine handles session lifecycle: MP+STATE_INITIAL (unused), MP+STATE_IDLE (active but no operation in progress), MP+STATE_ADD (adding channels), MP+STATE_REMOVE (removing channels), and MP+STATE_CLOSE (terminating). Each state and event pair determines actions: starting calls, incrementing counters, transitioning to the next state, or reporting errors.

Events triggering state changes include session start/termination from PPP/MP, link utilization notifications, received control messages, timer expirations, and call completion callbacks. The state machine ensures that both endpoints coordinate channel additions and removals in order.
sections.eli5: The connection follows a recipe: first exchange versions, then if someone wants to add or remove lines, both sides exchange request and response messages until the change completes.

sections.title: Operation and Device Management
sections.content:
MP+ negotiates itself as a PPP Link Control Protocol (LCP) option during initial connection setup, alongside the MP option. Both endpoints must agree to use MP before MP+ can be negotiated. Once negotiated, the MP+ process starts on the first connection.

Phone number management is a key feature: when the caller (call originator) requests to add channels via ADD_REQ with a count, the called endpoint (answerer) responds with ADD_RSP containing the actual phone numbers to dial. This eliminates the need for callers to know all possible phone numbers in advance.

Remote device management allows an operations center to dial into an unconfigured system, negotiate MP+, and issue remote management commands to configure ethernet interfaces, IP addresses, and other parameters before normal network configuration occurs. This requires only that WAN interfaces are minimally configured to answer calls.
sections.eli5: Both sides agree to use MP+ when they first connect. The called side can suggest phone numbers to add. A manager can also dial in and control a new device remotely before it is set up normally.
